title: What Happened When China Banned 24 Kinds of Scrap #shorts
summary: In July 2017 China notified the WTO it would ban 24 kinds of solid waste, including plastic scrap and mixed paper; what it still took faced a 0.5% contamination limit. US mixed paper exports to China fell 98.8% from Q1 2017 to Q1 2019 (USITC).
sources: China's policies, initially implemented in January 2018, include bans on mixed paper and contaminant limits of 0.5 percent on old corrugated containers and old newspapers; US exports to China of mixed paper decreased by 98.8 percent from Q1 2017 (575.6 thousand metric tons) to Q1 2019 (6.7 thousand metric tons); India and Indonesia partially filled the gap (US International Trade Commission, Executive Briefing on Trade, Nov 2019, S. Scott and R. Ireland): https://www.usitc.gov/publications/332/executive_briefings/ebot_trade_in_wastepaper.pdf

WTO notification G/TBT/N/CHN/1211, 18 July 2017: Catalogue of Solid Wastes Forbidden to Import into China by the End of 2017 (4 classes, 24 kinds), including plastic scrap, mixed paper waste, textile waste and vanadium slag (WTO TBT notification; copy hosted by UNEP): https://apps1.unep.org/resolutions/uploads/2017-world_trade_organization-chn1211_1.pdf
